finding.summary:
Hmm, I think there's a real bug here, not just a style nitpick like my other comments :-). If the `DeviceIoControl` call fails and the function exits early, then we can "lose" the `afd_group` -- it still has vacancies, but we won't put it back in `self._vacant_afd_groups`. I think the clearest way would be to leave the group in `_vacant_afd_groups` until we're ready to increment `.size`.

It's annoying there's no equivalent of `pop` that *doesn't* remove the item. I guess the choices are `afd_group = next(iter(self._vacant_afd_groups))` or `afd_group = self._vacant_afd_groups.pop(); self._vacant_afd_groups.add(afd_group)`.

label: real_issue
label_reason: A human reviewer raised this in python-trio/trio#1832 (merged 2020-12-29), and a later commit in the PR changes the file.
notes: Hand-picked with Claude Code (PMAT-310): https://github.com/python-trio/trio/pull/1832. Python: state is updated before a call that can fail, so a failure loses track of a resource. Human reviewers are not perfect ground truth, and they give no severity, so any severity counts.
